title: Render Contract
description: What the canonical renderer actually implements, per component render: the content props its branch reads, the fallback each prop has, and which of the registry's variant values it renders distinctly. Emitted by scripts/render/derive-contract.js into components/render/dist/render-contract.json. Consumers (the plugin's flow-authoring reference, the render content layer, the Claude Design bundle) read this instead of restating the same facts by hand, which is how a consumer's list of renderable components had drifted to 19 against the renderer's 58 by August 2026. Those two numbers are dated history, not a live claim about either side.

_meta.description: Provenance stamp carried by every generated JSON in this repo, so a reader can tell derived content from authored content.

examples.do_not_edit: Regenerate with `npm run derive:render`. Hand edits are overwritten.

auto_generated.description: Always true: this file is regenerated by CI and hand edits do not survive.

source.description: The inputs this contract was derived from, so a stale contract can be traced to the file that moved.

do_not_edit.description: The command that regenerates this file, printed where an editor will see it.
examples: Regenerate with `npm run derive:render`. Hand edits are overwritten.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this contract envelope shape, bumped when the structure changes so a vendored consumer can detect a shape it cannot read.

generatedBy.description: Repo-relative path of the derive script that produced this contract, for provenance.

slugs.description: One entry per render slug, keyed by slug. The key set is exactly the set of `case "<slug>":` branches in the renderer, so a component cannot be present here without being renderable.

group.description: The component's registry category, used as the grouping label by gallery consumers such as the Claude Design bundle's @dsCard marker.

props.description: Every content prop this renderer branch reads, sorted by name. A prop absent from this list is ignored by the renderer, so an author who sets it gets an empty slot rather than an error.

name.description: The prop name, case-sensitive and matching the renderer exactly. May contain spaces, e.g. "Placeholder text".

default.description: The literal the renderer falls back to when the prop is absent. Omitted when the fallback is the empty string, because an empty default is the absence of one rather than guidance to render nothing. Also omitted, and this is a known limit rather than a statement about the renderer, when the fallback is reached through a variable or through a non-prop operand (`props.App || v["App type"] || "Studio"`): resolving those would mean following identifiers through the renderer, and a wrong default is worse than a missing one because a content layer can author what is missing but will trust what is wrong. So read an absent default as "this derive cannot see one", never as "the renderer has none".

variants.description: One entry per registry variant axis, keyed by the axis name exactly as the registry spells it (the renderer keys on that spelling, e.g. button uses "State" and text-input uses "States").

values.description: The axis values the registry publishes, in registry order.

rendersAs.description: Values the renderer cannot tell apart, mapped to the earlier value of the same axis they render identically to. Measured by rendering each value and comparing the markup, so it is empty for an axis the renderer fully honours and self-corrects when the renderer learns a difference. A consumer should treat a listed value as decoration: selecting it changes the label and nothing else.

additionalProperties.description: The value that this one renders identically to.
